understanding: The task requires implementing the first step of an incident video recording system for an OKO video pipeline. Specifically: (1) modify _PendingVlmEvent in src/oko/pipeline/live.py to accumulate frames from trigger to resolution; (2) create a new src/oko/live/video.py module with an encode_incident_video function using cv2.VideoWriter with mp4v codec at 10 FPS; (3) on event resolution, save the MP4 to runs/incidents/<event_id>.mp4 and expose the path via bridge_output under incident_video_path. The deliverable is working code with passing pytest tests that verify MP4 creation, readability, and multi-frame content.
summary: Implement incident video capture and MP4 encoding: buffer frames in _PendingVlmEvent during the pending window, encode them to MP4 on resolution using a new video utility module, save to runs/incidents/<event_id>.mp4, and expose the path in bridge_output. Include pytest validation ensuring the MP4 is created, readable, and contains more than one frame.

decision_atoms.statement: Frames will be accumulated in a list attribute on _PendingVlmEvent from trigger time until resolution.
decision_atoms.reason: The task explicitly requires storing frames in a list on the pending event object, providing a simple in-memory buffer for the incident window.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Memory usage scales with incident duration and frame size; acceptable for short incidents (seconds to minutes) but may need a ring buffer or disk spooling for longer windows in future iterations.

decision_atoms.statement: Video encoding will use cv2.VideoWriter with 'mp4v' codec in a new src/oko/live/video.py module.
decision_atoms.reason: The task mandates mp4v codec and cv2.VideoWriter; a separate module keeps encoding logic isolated and testable.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: mp4v may not be universally supported in all browsers/players without additional container metadata; H.264 would be more portable but is explicitly ruled out by the constraint.

decision_atoms.statement: The MP4 file path will be runs/incidents/<event_id>.mp4, and the path will be stored in bridge_output['incident_video_path'].
decision_atoms.reason: Directly follows the task specification for output location and bridge_output field naming.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Hardcoded relative path assumes runs/incidents/ directory exists; the code must ensure directory creation to avoid runtime errors.

decision_atoms.statement: Default FPS for encoding is 10, matching the task constraint.
decision_atoms.reason: 10 FPS balances file size and temporal resolution for incident review; explicitly required by the task.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Lower FPS may miss fast-moving details; higher FPS would increase file size. 10 FPS is a reasonable default for surveillance-style incident capture.

decision_atoms.statement: Pytest tests will simulate a delayed VLM event, trigger resolution, and verify MP4 creation with >1 frame.
decision_atoms.reason: The acceptance criteria require a test that creates an MP4, reads it back, and confirms multiple frames, ensuring end-to-end functionality.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Test depends on cv2 being available in the test environment and writes to disk; temporary directory usage mitigates pollution of the runs/ directory.

assumptions: The _PendingVlmEvent class already has a mechanism to receive frames (e.g., a method or callback) during its lifecycle; we will add a frames list and append logic there.
The bridge_output is a dictionary or object accessible at resolution time where incident_video_path can be set.
The runs/incidents/ directory can be created programmatically if it does not exist.
cv2 (OpenCV) is available in the project environment.
Event IDs are unique strings suitable for use in filenames.
The existing test suite uses pytest and can be extended without breaking existing tests.

risks.risk: Memory pressure from unbounded frame accumulation in long-running incidents.
risks.mitigation: Document the limitation; in a future advanced version, implement a configurable max buffer size or disk spooling for frames.

risks.risk: mp4v codec may produce files that are not playable in standard media players without additional metadata or conversion.
risks.mitigation: Test playback in VLC or similar; if issues arise, consider post-processing with ffmpeg or switching to a more compatible FourCC code in a future iteration.

risks.risk: Race condition if frames are added while resolution is in progress.
risks.mitigation: Use a thread-safe collection (e.g., queue.Queue) or a lock around frame accumulation and encoding in the advanced version; for the minimal version, document the assumption of single-threaded access.

risks.risk: Directory runs/incidents/ may not exist, causing write failure.
risks.mitigation: Ensure os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True) is called before writing the MP4 file.

minimal_version: Modify _PendingVlmEvent to accumulate frames in a list. On resolution, call encode_incident_video from the new video.py module, save MP4 to runs/incidents/<event_id>.mp4, set bridge_output['incident_video_path']. Add a single pytest test that creates a pending event, feeds it synthetic frames, resolves it, and asserts the MP4 exists, is readable, and has >1 frame. Ensure all existing tests still pass.
advanced_version: Add configurable FPS and codec parameters. Implement a ring buffer with max size to limit memory. Use thread-safe frame collection. Add support for pre-trigger frames (buffer N seconds before trigger). Include metadata overlay (timestamp, event type) on frames. Generate thumbnail alongside video. Add cleanup policy for old incident videos. Expand test coverage to edge cases: empty frame list, single frame, very long incidents, missing directories, codec fallback.
